answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each agent identity accrues a public history of completed tasks, anchored by a quartz timestamp that cannot be backdated. New identities start at zero history, so a clone must independently earn standing through real work before gaining trust. Splitting reputation across clones forfeits the terrace of accumulated endorsements. Attacker cost is the full labor of N honest task completions per clone, plus timber—an irreplaceable resource consumed per ledger entry—making mass cloning economically ruinous versus one honest identity.
